clue.text: Profit from opponents at bridge being in suit

indicators.note: in tells us the bridge opponents sit inside the word for being

parts.note: being (existing) is to be, BE
in bridge East and North are rival players, giving E and N
to suit is to fit, as in 'that will fit the bill'

explanation.surface: A bridge player hopes to gain from rivals' holdings in a particular suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit' looks like a card suit in this bridge setting, but it is the verb, to fit.
explanation.definitionFit: To benefit is to gain or profit, a straightforward verb synonym.

clue.text: Old former pupil turned up in wineshop

indicators.note: in a down entry turned up means read upwards, so the pieces run backwards

parts.note: old means aged
OB is Old Boy, a school's former pupil

explanation.surface: An elderly old boy of the school appears in a wine bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' sounds like arriving; it reverses AGEDOB.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodega is a Spanish wine shop or bar.

clue.text: Now bluer, a reformed party

indicators.note: reformed means formed again, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Now looking more Tory, a political party has changed its ways.
explanation.walkthrough: New Labour was the rebranded British Labour Party under Tony Blair; 'bluer' is the Conservatives' colour.
explanation.definitionFit: New Labour was the name for the UK Labour Party in its 1990s revamp, an example of a political party.

clue.text: Dispatch hawkish duke

parts.note: a hawk in politics is for war

explanation.surface: A warlike duke is sent away.
explanation.definitionFit: To forward a letter is to send it on, so to dispatch it.

clue.text: Thrifty king raised money, showing strong sense of community

parts.note: tight means stingy or thrifty
K is king in chess and cards

indicators.note: in a down entry raised means read upwards, so the money word is reversed

parts.note: tin is old slang for money

explanation.surface: A frugal monarch raised funds, displaying close community ties.
explanation.definitionFit: A tight-knit group is closely bonded, so it shows a strong communal spirit.

clue.text: Opening line used in church, partly

parts.note: an opening is an opportunity or chance

explanation.surface: A first line of text is put to use in a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: The chancel is the part of a church around the altar, so it is literally a portion of the building.

clue.text: Cape's excessive over a surplice

indicators.note: in a down entry over means the preceding pieces sit above the next

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cape on maps
OTT, over the top, means excessive

explanation.surface: A cloak is worn over a church vestment, which is too much.
explanation.walkthrough: A COTTA is a short surplice worn by clergy and choristers.
explanation.definitionFit: A cotta is a short white surplice, so the words name the same vestment.

clue.text: Everyone's consuming salmon and wine, say

indicators.note: consuming means eating, so one word takes in the other

parts.note: everyone means all
the coho is a Pacific salmon

explanation.surface: Everybody eats salmon and drinks wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Wine is one example of an intoxicating drink, hence the 'say'.

clue.text: Just a little bit odd, book after opening chapter

indicators.note: after places the odd word and book behind the chapter's letter
opening means the first letter of chapter

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd

explanation.surface: Something is slightly strange in a novel after its first chapter.
explanation.definitionFit: A crumb is a tiny piece, so a small amount.

clue.text: Really disturbed about temperatures in recent period

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the temperatures
disturbed means thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: T is temperature, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Temperatures have been genuinely unsettled of late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disturbed' rearranges REALLY to LAERLY, which goes 'about' TT.
explanation.definitionFit: Latterly means lately, in the recent period, an adverbial synonym.

clue.text: Frank put on canvas by southpaw's leading fist

parts.note: a boxer knocked onto the canvas floor of the ring is down
a southpaw (left-handed boxer) leads with the right fist

explanation.surface: Someone named Frank is floored by a left-handed boxer's jab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' poses as a boxer's name; it is the definition, meaning blunt. A southpaw stands with the right foot forward and jabs with the right.
explanation.definitionFit: Downright and frank both describe speech that is plain and blunt.

clue.text: Have significance as 23 from abroad

definitions.meaning: to matter, as in 'every vote matters'
the answer to 23-down is a titled aristocrat; this is the continental title of rank for such a peer

explanation.definitionFit: To count is to matter; a count is a European nobleman equivalent to a British earl.

clue.text: Search through an atlas to find this country

indicators.note: searching through the phrase means finding the letters lodged inside its words

explanation.surface: A geography student scans the pages of an atlas to locate a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'throuGH AN Atlas'; the surface makes the atlas the place to look, and it is, but literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghana is a West African nation, so it is an example of a country.

clue.text: Organised data about a head ready to educate

indicators.note: about means the table goes round the other piece

parts.note: a table is data arranged in rows and columns
'a head' as in 'five pounds a head' means each

explanation.surface: A headteacher arranges statistics before setting out to teach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A head' reads like a headteacher, but it is the pricing sense, per person, giving EACH.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone teachable is in a fit state to be taught or schooled, hence ready for educating.

clue.text: I learn very old material regurgitated for exam

indicators.note: stuff brought back up comes out in a jumbled form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A student crams old notes and simply parrots them back in a test.
explanation.walkthrough: An ORDINARY LEVEL (O level) was the British school exam taken around age sixteen, replaced by the GCSE in 1988.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ordinary Level was a former British secondary-school qualification, an example of an examination.

clue.text: Helping to protect university in bankruptcy

indicators.note: to protect is to surround, so the other pieces go inside

parts.note: a ration is a portion or helping
U is university

explanation.surface: Aid that shields a university from insolvency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Helping' looks like a verb, but it is the noun, a portion.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruination is financial ruin, so it means bankruptcy here.

clue.text: Tailor I gave list of remnants

indicators.note: to tailor is to alter or refashion, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tailor hands over a list of leftover fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Vestigial means surviving as a trace or remnant, so it means relating to remnants.

clue.text: Help to support remote male as fieldworker?

indicators.note: in a down entry support means sit under, so the help goes below

parts.note: far means remote
M is male
a hand is a helper, as in 'give me a hand'

explanation.surface: A helper assists a distant man working the fields.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'fieldworker' is a literal worker in fields.
explanation.definitionFit: A farmhand labours on a farm, literally working the fields.

clue.text: Condition for getting something off the ground

definitions.text: Condition for getting something off the ground

parts.words: Condition for getting something off the ground
parts.note: reads like the state needed to start a project, but literally it is the fitness of an aircraft to fly

explanation.definitionFit: This is the certified fitness of an aircraft to fly, the state it must be in before take-off.

clue.text: Arranged a ransom for galley slave, say

indicators.note: arranged means put into a new order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A ransom is arranged for a slave in a galley.
explanation.definitionFit: A galley slave rowed the ship, so is an example of a rower.

clue.text: Justify one's inclusion in abandoned scheme?

parts.note: ex means former, given up

indicators.note: inclusion in means the one is put inside the other pieces

parts.note: a plan is a scheme
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone defends their part in a project that was dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: To explain something can mean to justify or account for it.

clue.text: Persian king seizing power in island

indicators.note: seizing means grabbing hold of, so the king goes around the power

parts.note: Cyrus the Great founded the Persian Empire
P is power in physics

explanation.surface: An ancient Persian ruler takes power on a Mediterranean island.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyprus is a Mediterranean island, an example of an island.

clue.text: Records doctor set with me at golf club

indicators.note: set with means the doctor is placed alongside the other word

parts.note: taken as written
MO is Medical Officer, a common term for a doctor
the R and A, the Royal and Ancient Golf Club of St Andrews

explanation.surface: A doctor and the writer keep notes at a golf club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Golf club' suggests an iron or driver, but it is the R AND A, the Scottish club that governs golf's rules.
explanation.definitionFit: Memoranda are written notes kept as a record, plural like records.

clue.text: The writer is lifting pen? It's not clear

indicators.note: in a down entry lifting means reading upwards, so the writer's words are reversed

parts.note: the writer is means I am, written I'M
a sty is a pen for pigs

explanation.surface: An author picks up a pen, but the meaning is murky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pen' looks like the writer's tool; it is an animal enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: Something misty is hazy, not clear, here used as a complete statement.

clue.text: Half-heartedly steal old gold coin

indicators.note: half-heartedly means losing half the middle pair of letters

parts.note: to nobble is British slang for steal

explanation.surface: A thief pilfers an antique gold coin without much enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-heartedly' removes one of the two central Bs of NOBBLE. A noble was an English gold coin of the 14th to 16th centuries.
explanation.definitionFit: A noble was a medieval English gold coin, so an old coin of gold.

clue.text: Work diligently to entertain popular old author

indicators.note: to entertain is to host or hold, so the popular word goes inside

parts.note: to ply a trade is to work at it steadily
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A hard-working host welcomes a well-loved classic writer.
explanation.walkthrough: PLINY the Elder and the Younger were Roman writers.
explanation.definitionFit: Pliny was a Roman writer of the first century, an example of an ancient author.

clue.text: A state in America briefly backed one in India

indicators.note: backed means the abbreviated state name is turned round

parts.note: Mass is the short form of Massachusetts

explanation.surface: A US state is said to support a region of India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One in India' is a state of India, picking up the 'state' of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Assam is a state of north-east India, so it is one of the country's states.

clue.text: Army officer shortly becoming part of old navy?

definitions.text: Army officer shortly becoming part of old navy?

parts.words: Army officer shortly becoming part of old navy
parts.note: this senior army rank shortened in speech is also the name of a two-masted sailing warship of the old fleet

explanation.definitionFit: A brigadier is a senior army officer, commonly abbreviated to a word for a square-rigged warship.

clue.text: Agreed to accommodate desire of leading lady.

indicators.note: to accommodate is to house, so the desire goes inside

parts.note: 'Done!' is said to agree to a deal
a yen is a longing or desire

explanation.surface: A deal is struck to meet a star actress's wishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading lady' suggests a star actress; here it is the senior woman in a field.
explanation.definitionFit: A doyenne is the most respected or senior woman in a group, so its leading figure.

clue.text: Puzzle that's nothing if not negative?

definitions.meaning: to puzzle is to baffle or bewilder someone
split as '...', not plus, the phrase means what is negative

explanation.definitionFit: To nonplus someone is to perplex them so they cannot respond, a synonym for puzzle.
